testEnvironment:
Test environment: the snapshot is a git repository whose single commit holds
the reviewed tree — its tree hash was compared against the commit under review
when the snapshot was cut. A suite run here collects and runs what a checkout at
that commit does, so a failing or skipped test is a fact about the tree, not
about this copy of it. Its history is that one synthetic commit: 'git log',
'git diff' and every ancestry question answer about the snapshot and never about
the PR.
The Recipe's Test entrypoint and Check step do not run these merge-gating CI steps, and nothing in this review ran them: rebase-check job (pull_request-only branch-currency assertion, not meaningful in a worktree of origin/main); proc-macos job (node --test tests/proc.test.mjs on macOS) (subsumed by the full suite on this macOS host); smoke-omp job (needs pinned omp installed via bun, absent here); install-and-smoke job (needs pinned omp installed via bun and network, absent here).

The read tool reports test-run.log at /Users/chris/.fleet/scratch/fleet-plugin-28971265/pr4411/run-nTj1T7vR/ as not found, so the redirect never opened and no TEST_RUN_EXIT or summary was produced. unverified.claim: No logic error found: both new tests pass on the unmutated tree and each kills the mutant the ticket names (G kills only test 14, H kills only test 15), so the PR does what #4405 asks.
unverified.evidence: Narrowed run in the measuring copy (`node --test --test-reporter=tap --test-name-pattern='^alarm:' tests/phase0.test.mjs`). Unmutated: exit 0, tests 18, pass 18. G (`fleetIdentity(rec.fleet) !== fleetDir`): exit 1, fail 1, 'not ok 14 - alarm: phase 0's own .fleet/ spelled through a symlink…'. H (`return realpathSync(dirname(path))`): exit 1, fail 1, 'not ok 15 - alarm: a file naming another directory of this checkout is refused…'. Controls: Gb (`rec.fleet !== fleetIdentity(fleetDir)`) fails test 13. K (`return realpathSync(path)`) fails tests 13 and 14. Whole file: exit 0, tests 114, pass 114.

unverified.claim: Test 14 depends on git printing an absolute GIT_COMMON_DIR exactly as spelled. The test checks this itself: its output assertion `join(link, ".fleet")` fails if git ever canonicalises the path, so the test can go red but can never pass without testing anything. I measured this only on Apple Git 2.54.0, not on CI's Linux git.
unverified.evidence: Test 14 passed on git 2.54.0 (Apple Git-157), with its receipt output equal to `controller alarm armed: pid …, <link>/.fleet`, so fleetDir was spelled through the link. Mutant G turned that test red, so the non-canonical side was really exercised. Linux git was not run.
unverified.suggested_fix: None required. If CI on another git version ever fails here, the output assertion is the place to look.

unverified.claim: The refusal half of test 14 checks the exit code and the stdout line but not `receipt().steps.alarm.status === "failed"`, which test 15 and the existing test 16 both check. This is a small inconsistency, not a correctness gap, because exit 3 plus the `alarm: failed` line already pin the refusal.
unverified.evidence: Read tests/phase0.test.mjs:583-585 against :596-598 and :611-613 in the snapshot. No mutant was built that this omission would let survive.
unverified.suggested_fix: Optionally add `assert.equal(f.receipt().steps.alarm.status, "failed");` after line 585 so it matches its neighbours.

unverified.claim: No scope creep: the diff adds only two tests to tests/phase0.test.mjs and changes no production code, fixture helpers or other tests, which matches the ticket's 'Candidate remedy'.
unverified.evidence: Read pr.diff whole (46 lines): it has one `diff --git` header (tests/phase0.test.mjs), one hunk `@@ -564,6 +564,41 @@`, and every changed line is an addition.

unverified.claim: Both new tests discriminate: the symlinked-own-spelling test is killed by dropping realpath and by basename-only, and the other-directory test is killed by dropping basename or by prefix matching, each uniquely.
unverified.evidence: red: ./agent-test tests/phase0.test.mjs (mutant: fleetIdentity returns path) → exit 1, fail 2 incl alarm: phase 0's own .fleet/ spelled through a symlink is the same .fleet/ as the file's real spelling…; baseline: ./agent-test tests/phase0.test.mjs → exit 0, tests 114, pass 114 (full-suite runs, narrowing unprovable). red: same cmd (mutant: basename-only) → exit 1, fail 3 incl the same new test. red: same cmd (mutant: realpath(dirname) without basename) → exit 1, fail 1 incl alarm: a file naming another directory of this checkout is refused, through a symlink or not. red: same cmd (mutant: startsWith instead of !==) → exit 1, fail 1 incl the same test.

unverified.claim: PR body and commit 12baab01: the statements that each new test 'fails under its mutant' (fleetIdentity with no realpath, fleetIdentity dropping the .fleet basename, and the compare) are unverified. I could not run any mutation in this review.
unverified.evidence: I read the code and the tests. fleetIdentity (phase0.mjs:606-610) canonicalises with join(realpathSync(dirname(path)), basename(path)). The compare is at phase0.mjs:650. The new test cases are consistent with those mutants: GIT_COMMON_DIR through the link gives a non-canonical fleetDir, and `fleet`/`other` paths differ in basename or directory. Bash was broken, so no mutant was executed. The '114 of 114' count agrees with the static count (79 top-level tests plus 35 REFUSALS entries = 114), but that is a count of tests, not a pass result.
unverified.suggested_fix: Have the main agent run the two new tests against the two mutants in its own copy to confirm the claim.

unverified.claim: The comment at tests/phase0.test.mjs:571, 'An absolute GIT_COMMON_DIR is the way git answers `--git-common-dir` as spelled, so phase 0 derives its own `.fleet/` through the link', is plausible but not shown by any run in this review.
unverified.evidence: Static read only. fleetDir comes from fleetFile(null) at phase0.mjs:745. GIT_ENV scrubs only GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE and GH_REPO (tests lines 34-37), so GIT_COMMON_DIR reaches the child. The test's own assertion at line 578, that the output is `join(link, ".fleet")`, would fail if the claim were wrong.
unverified.suggested_fix: No change needed if the full file run is green.
